A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same DOLPHIN framework and contain readable main text and Appendices A–H. Their text, equations, tables, and rendered figures support reliable comparison, including material moved or renumbered.

before.justification: V2 reports original benchmark accuracies and training times in Section 4, plus provenance comparisons, execution analyses, and MNIST ProductN experiments in the appendices.

after.justification: V4 retains original benchmark results and reports additional no-timeout accuracy comparisons and top-K sensitivity results in Appendix D.

M1.justification: The Distribution abstraction, five primitives, CPU/GPU division, DAMP and DTKP-AM provenances, and training objective remain unchanged. The added worked examples and object-detection illustration explain applications of existing operations rather than introduce a new method component.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same SumN, HWF, PathFinder, CLUTRR, and Mugen variants, including the additional ProductN experiments in Appendix G. The new timeout and K studies reuse existing coverage. The autonomous-driving discussion provides no evaluated dataset or task.

E2.justification: Comparator participation remains Scallop across the benchmark suite, ISED and IndeCateR+ on SumN/HWF, and LTN on SumN. The DAMP-versus-DTKP-AM comparison is retained. Newly discussed SLASH and A-NESI are not experimentally evaluated.

E3.justification: Sections 4.2–4.3 change the stated 10-hour timeout to a soft threshold and report runs exceeding it. Appendix D.2 adds evaluation until convergence or test-accuracy plateau alongside the capped comparison. Appendix D.3 introduces a K = 1, 3, 5, 7 sweep across five benchmarks; these are additional protocols, not changes to the documented default K settings.

E4.justification: V4 adds substantial analyses of whether baseline accuracy deficits persist without the time limit and how DTKP-AM accuracy/runtime depend on K. Conversely, v2's Mugen convergence diagnostics, comprising Figures 8–9 and Appendix D.7, are removed. The existing provenance and ProductN analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Both Section 4.2 descriptions specify three runs and averages of best accuracy and training time. Accuracy plots retain error bars. No new seed protocol, uncertainty definition, confidence interval, or significance-testing procedure is documented.

E6.justification: Tables 2–3 replace multiple timeout entries with numerical runtimes. Table 2 revises Mugen-1K times from 3.81e3/1.34e4 seconds for DOLPHIN/Scallop to 2.39e3/6.71e3, while Figure 5 substantially raises Scallop's reported Mugen accuracies. Table 5 corrects SumN-5 entries, including Scallop's ratio from 3.43 to 17.16. New no-timeout and K-sweep results expand the evidence; Table 6 reports HWF-19 accuracy of 8.94% at K=1 and 99.15% at K=3. These additions and revisions do not establish a same-setting improvement of the proposed method.

T1.justification: The formal primitives, provenance definitions, training equation, and Appendix A reasoning are retained. Examples 3.1–3.4 instantiate existing operations. Appendix A.1 repairs incomplete provenance naming without changing its derivation or mathematical conclusion.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contribution list, and conclusion retain the same substantive claims about scalable Python/PyTorch neurosymbolic programming, vectorized provenances, and performance across 13 benchmarks. The headline 1.71x–62x speedup claim also remains.

C2.justification: Section 4.4 materially qualifies the accuracy narrative: IndeCateR+'s HWF-19 deficit is attributed to training time, and some baselines are acknowledged to match DOLPHIN without a timeout. The Mugen advantage discussion and proposed backend explanation for its convergence gap are removed. New Section 5 develops applicability arguments through object detection, while Appendix D.3 interprets K sensitivity. The concluding limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: V4 newly supplies a DOLPHIN code-repository address and states that HWF/MNIST use Scallop's CNN architecture. It additionally specifies CLUTRR's pretrained roberta-base fine-tuning configuration and a three-layer ReLU CNN for MNIST. These are documentation additions; the PDFs do not establish corresponding architecture changes.

R1.justification: Related work adds SLASH and A-NESI, describing pruning and learned approximation as alternative scalability strategies. Existing citations and the general positioning against constrained or inefficient neurosymbolic frameworks are otherwise retained.

P1.justification: V4 adds four worked examples, a Discussion section, and acknowledgements, and locally revises experimental prose and reorganizes Appendix D. Most existing exposition and the overall method-to-experiments narrative remain intact, so this is a limited expansion rather than extensive rewriting.

P2.justification: The experimental displays are substantially revised: v4 adds the no-timeout Figure 7 and K-sweep Tables 6–7, removes v2's Mugen Figures 8–9, and changes Figure 5's sizing and axis ticks. Runtime tables highlight numerical values exceeding 10 hours instead of timeout markers. The SumN architecture and provenance plots are retained under new numbers, alongside conference-format header and caption changes.

improvement.justification: The no-timeout comparison and K sweep better support interpretation of efficiency and parameter sensitivity, while worked examples and code/model documentation improve usability. Gains are tempered by removal of Mugen diagnostic curves and incomplete reconciliation of revised results: Section 4.3 still describes larger Mugen as exceeding the baselines' 10-hour reach, although Table 2 now reports Scallop's Mugen-5K time as 3.59e4 seconds, below that threshold. The net improvement is useful but limited.
